findings.summary: With queries read inside the main loop, an `@alt(program)` brute is refused even for plain input values like `n`, `a`, `q` (`is the solution's own work`), so I had to restructure the solution to read all queries up front.
findings.evidence: sol/drafts/cf2285D_alt_reads_in_loop.cp: main reads `for _ in 0..q: let i: 1..=n = read()`; `cpl check` -> error[E0201]: `n` is the solution's own work: a brute or a checker shares only the input --> cf2285D.cp:44:37 (x9, also q, a, comb) help: it sees every top-level line down to the last `read()`; fixed by `let qs: [0..q](i: 1..=n, v: Int) = read()` at top level
